messages:
Maria Chen: FYI ap-southeast2 telemetry started dropping at ~12:07 UTC, seeing a surge of prometheus scrape errors and the GPU autoscaler lost KV cache metrics.
SRE Oncall Bot: Incident detected: prometheus-scrape-failure in ap-southeast2 — triggering P2 runbook.
Kevin O'Neill: I can see repeated egress failures from metric-collector: `dial tcp 13.52.x.x:443: i/o timeout` and a bunch of 429s from our telemetry ingest. Likely NAT/gateway throttling.
Anya Patel: That would explain missing traces and logs — if exporters can't reach ingest, Prom will mark targets as failed and autoscaler becomes blind.
Maria Chen: Logs excerpt from metric-collector: ```
time="2026-03-18T12:06:58Z" level=error msg="post telemetry failed" err="HTTP 429 Too Many Requests"
time="2026-03-18T12:07:02Z" level=warn msg="egress dial timeout" err="i/o timeout"
```
Luis Gomez: Confirmed with cloud console — NAT gateway showing spikes in connections and hitting soft limit for concurrent egress flows in that region.
Kevin O'Neill: Quick mitigation idea: enable a lightweight local fallback for metric-collector that writes minimal metrics to cluster logging and extends scrape timeout. We can flip an env var and scale the daemonset.
Ops Runbook Bot: Runbook step: if telemetry egress blocked -> enable TELEMETRY_FALLBACK, increase replicas to 5, increase prometheus scrape_timeout to 20s, and notify cloud provider.
Maria Chen: I'm going to apply the fallback and bump the replicas now: `kubectl -n infra set env ds/metric-collector TELEMETRY_FALLBACK=1 && kubectl scale ds/metric-collector --replicas=5 -n infra && kubectl rollout restart ds/metric-collector -n infra`
Kevin O'Neill: Applying the commands. Patching ds and restarting pods (rolling).
Kevin O'Neill: Pods are back up with TELEMETRY_FALLBACK=1. Collector logs show fallback active: `metrics_fallback=true, mode=local-buffer`.
Maria Chen: Prometheus target errors dropping from ~18/s to ~1/s in the last 90s. Grafana KV cache hitrate recovered to baseline. Autoscaler is seeing metrics again and started provisioning paused pools.
Anya Patel: Next steps: open provider support ticket to raise NAT egress capacity and request quota increase. Also add a small regional egress jumpbox/gateway as a temporary dedicated route for telemetry.
Luis Gomez: I'll spin up a tiny static NAT gateway in ap-southeast2 as a stopgap and route telemetry through it.
Kevin O'Neill: I'll create a quick PR to: 1) add TELEMETRY_FALLBACK env var to the daemonset with default off, 2) emit `metrics_fallback=true` tag in logs/metrics when active, and 3) bump scrape_timeout to 20s in prometheus scrape config. Link: https://git.redwood/internal/infra/metric-collector/pull/432
Maria Chen: Also logging change: have collector emit an event to cluster-event-log when fallback flips so we can alert on fallback usage.
Anya Patel: Long-term items: regional telemetry endpoints, resilient buffering (disk-backed queue), and automated provider quota monitoring to preempt throttles.
Maria Chen: TL;DR cause = provider NAT egress throttling -> telemetry blackout -> autoscaler blind -> degraded GPU provisioning. Mitigation = enable collector fallback, scale ds, config tweaks, regional egress gateway, and provider ticket.
Kevin O'Neill: I'll follow up with the PR and RFC for disk-backed buffer.
Maria Chen: Thanks all — I'll update the incident postmortem with timeline and actions. :thumbsup:
Ops Runbook Bot: Incident marked mitigated; monitoring for 1hr.
